original_card.question: Can the native P104 low-rank channel be completed with a legal, fully charged I-G/2 side correction?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 open next questions and its fixed local histogram; inspect why appending I-G/2 after source completion is not justified. #1991 supplies the checked native channel, not the missing correction.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one exact side-correction cut and bound its allowed cost from a favorable completed moment at a declared target. Stop or hand off if the necessary source/target access cannot be justified or even the optimistic total misses the target.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.

actual_scope: Exact rational rank lower bound and finite P104 end-cut correction: sparse B^T B factorization with eight arbitrary dirty Q registers, 208 exact rank-one frame transports, and 2,376 scalar additions. At m=9, W=280 the corrected rank mass 2,576 exceeds mW=2,520, with zero-saving moment 46/45>1. A direct-F9 endpoint rewrite has the same 208 rank increase. The fixed-trajectory span verifier replays 280 rational rows and pools every helper and other-target snapshot in each target's underlying frame subspace, treating basis conversion as free. It finds all 104 actual I-G/2 correction rows outside their pooled spans (ranks 177–181). The common correction-extension intersection has dimension 72 and is contained in every fixed span, so one added row direction cannot supply any correction for all targets. Each natural correction row C_j serves only its own target modulo the fixed span; no cross-target reuse occurs in that basis. No general fusion or supplier result is claimed. A chronological exact-chart correction word was then constructed from 1,248 fixed helper snapshots plus one X_t term per target. Its 1,352 correction additions use 208 rank mass; all 280 rows replay exactly and helpers restore. The terminal source-frame detours have the same paid profile as the direct-F9 screen, so the finite corrected invoice still has zero-saving moment 46/45>1.
scope_change_reason: The original end-cut construction failed the fixed-interface moment. The all-time pooled span then tested the actual correction rows rather than only the unit rows, and ruled out scalar additions from unchanged helper and target trajectories even with free basis conversion. Quotient screens excluded a single shared direction and several finite families of pairs. A stronger projection argument now gives a universal lower bound of 96 on the dimension of any shared row space H: for a checked 96-target subset, the union of the projected fixed spans has rank 8 and adjoining those correction rows gives rank 104. Exact pooled-span checks find a 97-dimensional H, spanned by 97 natural correction rows, that supplies all targets; the witness is checked directly against all 104 original pooled spans. Thus the fixed-trajectory algebraic minimum lies in [96,97], before chronological realization or pricing. The exact 1,352-add snapshot correction remains a separate chronological construction with 208 added rank mass and the same noncontracting profile.
bottleneck_link: The native P104 G/2 channel leaves 152 units of mW-rank-mass slack under its width-nine, 280-role interface. The exact end-cut correction consumes 208 rank mass and exceeds that slack by 56; this rules out this appended word under the fixed-interface moment before global hosting, but does not rule out fusion or a changed interface.
stop_rule: The appended end-cut candidate and direct-F9 endpoint rewrite are fully priced and fail the fixed-interface moment. Fixed-trajectory scalar retuning cannot supply any I-G/2 row. The fixed pooled-span problem now has an exact dimension bracket 96<=k<=97, with a directly checked 97-dimensional correction-row witness but no chronological realization or favorable paid profile. Resolve whether k=96 is possible, then determine whether the corresponding space can be produced chronologically at lower rank mass. The separate 1,352-add snapshot correction is exact but has the same 208 rank-mass increase and fails the same fixed-interface moment; also consider a changed interface.
evidence: RESULT.json records rank(G)=8, rank(I-G/2)=104, det(2I-G), the 568-entry root-coordinate factorization, 2,376 correction additions, and the 2,576 rank mass versus mW=2,520. verify_transports.py checks all lifts/returns and direct-F9 endpoint operators including phase. verify_existing_delivery_span.py exactly replays 280 rows; confirms all 104 correction rows outside pooled fixed spans; computes the 72-dimensional common correction-extension intersection; screens all 66 natural-direction pairs, all 5,356 actual correction-row pairs and 1,248 mixed pairs; proves arbitrary-H lower bound 96 by exact projected ranks; and finds 121 covering spaces among 686 nearby 97-row correction-basis candidates, directly verifying one 97-dimensional witness against all 104 original pooled spans; tests all 97 single-row deletions from that witness, with best coverage 102 and no 96-dimensional witness in that local screen. SNAPSHOT-CORRECTION.json gives a chronological exact-chart word: 1,248 helper additions, 104 source-unit additions, 1,352 total, 208 rank mass. Exact 280-row replay restores all helpers and yields Y_t+X_t; verify_transports.py checks the terminal transport detour operators including phase and confirms the same paid profile/moment obstruction.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum dimension k of a shared added row space H such that every actual correction row C_t lies in S_t + H, and can such an H be realized chronologically by changed helper or carrier trajectories within a contracting paid profile?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact fixed-span minimum is now known to be 96 or 97. A directly checked 97-dimensional correction-row space covers all targets algebraically, but no chronological producer or improved paid invoice has been built.
open_questions.first_step: Search beyond single-row deletions of the recorded 97-row witness for a 96-dimensional correction-row basis or arbitrary 96-dimensional space, while retaining the universal projected lower-bound certificate; then try to realize a minimum space chronologically with lower rank mass.
open_questions.blocked_by: No shared multi-direction extension or chronological realization has been constructed.
